## Data S4: Supplementary File 4 Multiple sequence alignments and evaluation of variant-effect predictors.xlsx
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Data S4: Multiple sequence alignments and evaluation of VEPs
# ============================================================

# 1. Load required packages
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)


# 2. Define supplementary data file
file_path <- paste0(
  "./codes_Github_final/Supplementary_Data/",
  "Supplementary File 4 Multiple sequence alignments and evaluation of variant-effect predictors.xlsx"
)

# Check file exists
stopifnot(file.exists(file_path))


# 3. Load all worksheets into a named list
sheet_names <- readxl::excel_sheets(file_path)

data_s4 <- purrr::map(
  sheet_names,
  ~ readxl::read_excel(
    file_path,
    sheet = .x,
    guess_max = 10000
  )
)

names(data_s4) <- sheet_names


# 4. Inspect loaded datasets

# Available worksheets
names(data_s4)
#  [1] "Catalog"                    "VEP_predictor_metadata"     "VEP_protein_inputs"         "MSA_statistics"             "EVcouplings_mutations"      "EVcouplings_performance"    "VEP_sequence_scores"       
#  [8] "VEP_structure_scores"       "Evo2_genome_scores"         "Evo2_genome_performance"    "Evo2_ORF_scores"            "ESMIF1_single_vs_complex"   "ESMIF1_performance"         "VEP_performance_by_protein"
# [15] "VEP_performance_overall"   

# Dimensions of each worksheet
purrr::map(data_s4, dim)

# Column names of each worksheet
purrr::map(data_s4, names)

# Preview first rows
purrr::map(data_s4, head)


# 5. Check for import warnings
# Inspect column types in each worksheet
purrr::map(
  data_s4,
  ~ vapply(.x, class, character(1))
)




```



## Main analyses
Fig. 4G; Fig. S4D, E, F, G, J, K, L; 
### 1) VEP Performance summary (Fig. 4G; Fig. S4F)
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Data S4: VEP performance analysis
# ============================================================

# 1. Extract the two performance datasets
phix_vep_performance_by_protein <-
  data_s4[["VEP_performance_by_protein"]]

phix_vep_performance_overall <-
  data_s4[["VEP_performance_overall"]]


# 2. Inspect dimensions
dim(phix_vep_performance_by_protein)
dim(phix_vep_performance_overall)


# 3. Inspect column names
names(phix_vep_performance_by_protein)
names(phix_vep_performance_overall)


# 4. Preview
head(phix_vep_performance_by_protein)
head(phix_vep_performance_overall)



# ============================================================
# Prepare VEP performance plotting data
# ============================================================

# 1. Check required columns
required_cols <- c(
  "predictor_name",
  "gene_name",
  "median_rho"
)

stopifnot(
  all(required_cols %in%
        names(phix_vep_performance_by_protein))
)


# 2. Prepare data
#phix_perf_clean <-
  #phix_vep_performance_by_protein %>%
  #dplyr::filter(
    #!is.na(predictor_name),
    #!is.na(gene_name),
    #is.finite(median_rho)
  #)

# Exclude "TEM-1 (Control)"
phix_perf_clean <-
  phix_vep_performance_by_protein %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(predictor_name),
    !is.na(gene_name),
    gene_name != "TEM-1 (Control)",
    is.finite(median_rho)
  )


# 3. Check observations per predictor and protein
phix_perf_clean %>%
  dplyr::count(
    predictor_name,
    gene_name
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(n > 1)


# 4. Inspect predictors
sort(unique(phix_perf_clean$predictor_name))

# 5. Inspect proteins
sort(unique(phix_perf_clean$gene_name))
# [1] "A" "B" "C" "D" "E" "F" "G" "H" "J"


# ============================================================
# RSA baseline and predictor performance summary
# ============================================================

rsa_monomer <- "RSA (monomer)"
rsa_complex <- "RSA (complex)"


# 1. Median monomer RSA baseline
rsa_median_line <- phix_perf_clean %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    predictor_name == rsa_monomer
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    rsa_median = median(median_rho, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::pull(rsa_median)

print(rsa_median_line)


# 2. Prepare dot plotting data
phix_dot_plot_df <- phix_perf_clean %>%
  dplyr::group_by(predictor_name) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    predictor_median_rho = median(
      median_rho,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    n_proteins = dplyr::n_distinct(gene_name)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    predictor_name = forcats::fct_reorder(
      predictor_name,
      predictor_median_rho,
      .desc = TRUE
    ),

    is_rsa_monomer =
      as.character(predictor_name) == rsa_monomer,

    is_rsa_complex =
      as.character(predictor_name) == rsa_complex
  )


# 3. Summary by predictor
phix_model_median_df <- phix_dot_plot_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(predictor_name) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    model_median_rho = median(
      median_rho,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    n_proteins = dplyr::n_distinct(gene_name),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(phix_model_median_df)


# 4. Number-of-proteins labels
phix_n_label_df <- phix_dot_plot_df %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    predictor_name,
    n_proteins
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    y_pos = max(
      phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) + 0.04,

    n_label = paste0(
      "n=", n_proteins
    )
  )



# ============================================================
# Dot plot 1: VEP performance across proteins
# ============================================================

dot_plot_VEP_evaluation <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  #phix_dot_plot_df,
  phix_dot_plot_df[phix_dot_plot_df$gene_name != "TEM-1 (Control)",],
  
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = predictor_name,
    y = median_rho
  )
) +

  # Monomer RSA baseline
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = rsa_median_line,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  # Median performance per predictor
  ggplot2::stat_summary(
    fun = median,
    geom = "crossbar",
    width = 0.45,
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.35
  ) +

  # Other predictors
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    data = phix_dot_plot_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        !is_rsa_monomer,
        !is_rsa_complex
      ),
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    size = 1.4,
    alpha = 0.75,
    color = "black"
  ) +

  # Monomer RSA
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    data = phix_dot_plot_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(is_rsa_monomer),
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    size = 1.4,
    alpha = 0.85,
    color = "red"
  ) +

  # Complex RSA
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    data = phix_dot_plot_df %>%
      dplyr::filter(is_rsa_complex),
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    size = 1.4,
    alpha = 0.85,
    color = "orange"
  ) +

  # Number of proteins
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = phix_n_label_df,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = predictor_name,
      y = y_pos,
      label = n_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3,
    angle = 90,
    hjust = 0
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(
      floor(
        min(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE) * 10
      ) / 10,
      ceiling(
        (max(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.12) * 10
      ) / 10,
      by = 0.2
    ),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
  ) +

  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(
      min(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.12
    ),
    clip = "off"
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic() +

  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),

    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 15,
      r = 10,
      b = 10,
      l = 10
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Spearman rho",
    title = "ΦX174 predictor performance by protein",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Each dot is one protein; dashed line = median RSA (monomer), rho = ",
      round(rsa_median_line, 3)
    )
  )

print(dot_plot_VEP_evaluation)



# ============================================================
# Dot plot 2: VEP performance colored by protein
# ============================================================

dot_plot_VEP_evaluation_genes <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  phix_dot_plot_df,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = predictor_name,
    y = median_rho
  )
) +

  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = rsa_median_line,
    linetype = "dashed",

  ) +

  ggplot2::stat_summary(
    fun = median,
    geom = "crossbar",
    width = 0.45,

  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    ggplot2::aes(
      color = gene_name
    ),
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    size = 1.8,

  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = phix_n_label_df,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = predictor_name,
      y = y_pos,
      label = n_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3,
    angle = 90,
    hjust = 0
  ) +

  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(
      min(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.12
    ),
    clip = "off"
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic() +

  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),

    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 15,
      r = 10,
      b = 10,
      l = 10
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Spearman rho",
    color = "Protein",
    title = "ΦX174 predictor performance by protein",
    subtitle = paste0(
```

### 2) Correlations to single mutant matrics, Frequency and Conservation (Fig. S4G)
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Data S4: EVcouplings performance
# ============================================================

EVcouplings_performance <-
  data_s4[["EVcouplings_performance"]]

# Inspect data
dim(EVcouplings_performance)

names(EVcouplings_performance)

head(EVcouplings_performance)

# Inspect predictor and protein columns
dplyr::glimpse(EVcouplings_performance)



# ============================================================
# Prepare EVcouplings dot-plot dataframe
# ============================================================

EVcouplings_dot_plot_df <-
  EVcouplings_performance %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    result_type == "Protein",
    !is.na(protein),
    is.finite(performance_rho)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    gene_name = protein,

    predictor_name = factor(
      predictor_name,
      levels = c(
        "Frequency",
        "Conservation",
        "Independent model",
        "Epistatic model"
      )
    )
  )

# Inspect
EVcouplings_dot_plot_df %>%
  dplyr::select(
    gene_name,
    predictor_name,
    n_mutations,
    rho_raw,
    performance_rho
  )

# Check proteins and predictors
table(EVcouplings_dot_plot_df$predictor_name)
#         Frequency      Conservation Independent model   Epistatic model 
#                 9                 9                 9                 9 

sort(unique(EVcouplings_dot_plot_df$gene_name))
# [1] "A" "B" "C" "D" "E" "F" "G" "H" "J"



# ============================================================
# EVcouplings performance summary
# ============================================================

# 1. Calculate performance across proteins
EVcouplings_predictor_summary <-
  EVcouplings_dot_plot_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(predictor_name) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_proteins = dplyr::n_distinct(gene_name),

    median_rho = median(
      performance_rho,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    mean_rho = mean(
      performance_rho,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(EVcouplings_predictor_summary)
# # A tibble: 4 × 4
#   predictor_name    n_proteins median_rho mean_rho
#   <fct>                  <int>      <dbl>    <dbl>
# 1 Frequency                  9      0.255    0.206
# 2 Conservation               9      0.132    0.144
# 3 Independent model          9      0.196    0.204
# 4 Epistatic model            9      0.238    0.282


# 2. Determine plotting range
rho_min <- min(
  EVcouplings_dot_plot_df$performance_rho,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

rho_max <- max(
  EVcouplings_dot_plot_df$performance_rho,
  na.rm = TRUE
)


# 3. Prepare n labels
EVcouplings_n_label_df <-
  EVcouplings_predictor_summary %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_label = paste0("n = ", n_proteins),
    y_pos = rho_max + 0.06
  )


# ============================================================
# Dot plot 2: EVcouplings performance colored by protein
# ============================================================

dot_plot_EVcouplings_evaluation_genes <-
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    EVcouplings_dot_plot_df,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = predictor_name,
      y = performance_rho
    )
  ) +

  # Reference at zero
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  # RSA (monomer) baseline
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = rsa_median_line,
    color = "red",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  # Median performance
  ggplot2::stat_summary(
    fun = median,
    geom = "crossbar",
    width = 0.45,
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.35
  ) +

  # Points colored by protein
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(
    ggplot2::aes(
      color = gene_name
    ),
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    size = 1.8,
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +

  # Number of proteins
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = EVcouplings_n_label_df,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = predictor_name,
      y = y_pos,
      label = n_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3,
    angle = 90,
    hjust = 0
  ) +

  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(rho_min, rho_max + 0.12),
    clip = "off"
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic() +

  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 15, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Direction-adjusted Spearman rho",
    color = "Protein",
    title = expression(
      Phi*X174~alignment-derived~predictor~performance~(EVcouplings)
    ),
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Each dot is one protein\n",
      "Red crossbar = median across proteins\n",
      "Red dashed line = RSA (monomer), rho = ",
      round(rsa_median_line, 3)
    )
  )

print(dot_plot_EVcouplings_evaluation_genes)
```

### 3) Multiple sequence alignments, MSA (Fig. S4D, E)
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Data S4: MSA statistics
# ============================================================

phix_MSA_statistics <- data_s4[["MSA_statistics"]]

# Inspect columns and databases
names(phix_MSA_statistics)
#  [1] "protein"                 "database"                "bitscore"                "Meff"                    "Meff_L"                  "quality"                 "num_seqs"                "seqlen"                 
#  [9] "minimum_column_coverage" "num_cov"                 "perc_cov"                "len_cov"                 "selected_for_analysis"  

dim(phix_MSA_statistics)
# [1] 297  13

dplyr::glimpse(phix_MSA_statistics)

unique(phix_MSA_statistics$database)
# [1] "MGnify_UniProt" "UniRef100"      "UniRef90"  


# ============================================================
# Prepare MSA heatmap data
# ============================================================

msa_heatmap_data <- phix_MSA_statistics %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    database %in% c("UniRef100", "MGnify_UniProt")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    bitscore = factor(
      bitscore,
      levels = sort(unique(bitscore))
    )
  )

# Inspect
msa_heatmap_data %>%
  dplyr::count(database, protein)

# Check missing or failed alignment values
msa_heatmap_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.na(Meff_L))



# ============================================================
# Function: Plot MSA depth heatmap
# ============================================================

plot_MSA_Meff_heatmap <- function(
    df,
    database_name,
    plot_title
) {

  df_plot <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      database == database_name
    )

  ggplot2::ggplot(
    df_plot,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = bitscore,
      y = protein,
      
      #fill = log10(Meff + 1)
      fill = log10(Meff_L + 1)
      #fill = Meff_L
    )
  ) +

    # Heatmap tiles
    ggplot2::geom_tile(
      color = "white"
    ) +

    # Meff/L values
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      ggplot2::aes(
        label = round(Meff_L, 2)
      ),
      size = 4,
      color = "white"
    ) +

    ggplot2::theme_classic() +

    ggplot2::labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = "Bitscore threshold",
      y = "Proteins",
      fill = "Meff/L"
    )
}


# ============================================================
# MSA heatmap: UniRef100
# ============================================================

heatmap_MSA_Meff_UniRef100 <- plot_MSA_Meff_heatmap(
  df = msa_heatmap_data,

  database_name = "UniRef100",

  plot_title = paste0(
    "Alignment depth (Meff/L) in MSA using ",
    "EVcouplings (Database: UniRef100)"
  )
)

print(heatmap_MSA_Meff_UniRef100)
```

### 4) Evo2 variant scoring (Fig. S4J, K, L)
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Data S4: Evo2 genome variant scoring
# ============================================================

# 1. Extract supplementary datasets
Evo2_genome_performance <-
  data_s4[["Evo2_genome_performance"]]

Evo2_genome_scores <-
  data_s4[["Evo2_genome_scores"]]


# 2. Inspect dimensions
dim(Evo2_genome_performance)
dim(Evo2_genome_scores)


# 3. Inspect column names
names(Evo2_genome_performance)
names(Evo2_genome_scores)


# 4. Preview datasets
head(Evo2_genome_performance)
head(Evo2_genome_scores)


# 5. Inspect data types
dplyr::glimpse(Evo2_genome_performance)
dplyr::glimpse(Evo2_genome_scores)



# ============================================================
# Prepare Evo2 genome correlation bar-plot data
# ============================================================

# Check required columns
required_performance_cols <- c(
  "group",
  "base_pearson",
  "base_spearman",
  "micro_pearson",
  "micro_spearman"
)

stopifnot(
  all(required_performance_cols %in%
        names(Evo2_genome_performance))
)


# Convert wide-format performance results to long format
correlation_plot_data <-
  Evo2_genome_performance %>%
  dplyr::select(
    group,
    base_pearson,
    base_spearman,
    micro_pearson,
    micro_spearman
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -group,
    names_to = c("model", "method"),
    names_sep = "_",
    values_to = "correlation"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    group = factor(
      group,
      levels = c(
        "All variants",
        "1-nt",
        "2-nt",
        "3-nt"
      )
    ),

    model = dplyr::recode(
      model,
      base = "Evo2 (7B Base)",
      micro = "Evo2 (7B Microviridae)"
    ),

    method = factor(
      method,
      levels = c("spearman", "pearson"),
      labels = c("Spearman", "Pearson")
    )
  )

print(correlation_plot_data)



# ============================================================
# Function: Evo2 genome correlation bar plot
# ============================================================

plot_evo2_correlations <- function(
    data,
    correlation_method = "Spearman"
) {

  plot_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      method == correlation_method
    )

  ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = group,
      y = correlation,
      fill = model
    )
  ) +

    ggplot2::geom_col(
      position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.75),
      width = 0.65,
      color = NA
    ) +

    ggplot2::geom_text(
      ggplot2::aes(
        label = sprintf("%.3f", correlation)
      ),
      position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.75),
      vjust = -0.5,
      size = 3.5
    ) +

    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Evo2 (7B Base)" = "#0081D1",
        "Evo2 (7B Microviridae)" = "#F1BB3E"
      )
    ) +

    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 0.65),
      breaks = seq(0, 0.6, 0.1),
      expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
    ) +

    ggplot2::labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = paste0(correlation_method, " correlation"),
      fill = NULL
    ) +

    ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
        size = 11,
        color = "black"
      ),
      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(
        color = "black"
      ),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.justification = "center",
      legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title.y = ggplot2::element_text(size = 12)
    )
}


# ============================================================
# Plot 1: Spearman correlations (presented)
# ============================================================

p_evo2_spearman <- plot_evo2_correlations(
  correlation_plot_data,
  correlation_method = "Spearman"
)

print(p_evo2_spearman)

# ============================================================
# Prepare Evo2 genome variant scatter-plot data
# ============================================================

# Check required columns
required_score_cols <- c(
  "genome_nt_mut_ham",
  "dms_replication_score",
  "evo2_7b_base",
  "evo2_7b_microviridae"
)

stopifnot(
  all(required_score_cols %in%
        names(Evo2_genome_scores))
)


# Convert Evo2 scores to long format
evo2_plot_data <-
  Evo2_genome_scores %>%
  dplyr::select(
    dplyr::any_of("genome_mut_ID_nt"),
    genome_nt_mut_ham,
    dms_replication_score,
    evo2_7b_base,
    evo2_7b_microviridae
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      evo2_7b_base,
      evo2_7b_microviridae
    ),
    names_to = "model",
    values_to = "evo2_score"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = dplyr::recode(
      model,
      evo2_7b_base = "Evo2 (7B Base)",
      evo2_7b_microviridae = "Evo2 (7B Microviridae)"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(evo2_score),
    is.finite(dms_replication_score)
  )


# Inspect data
dplyr::count(evo2_plot_data, model)
# # A tibble: 2 × 2
#   model                      n
#   <chr>                  <int>
# 1 Evo2 (7B Base)         44195
# 2 Evo2 (7B Microviridae) 44195

dplyr::count(
  evo2_plot_data,
  genome_nt_mut_ham,
  model
)
# # A tibble: 6 × 3
#   genome_nt_mut_ham model                      n
#               <dbl> <chr>                  <int>
# 1                 1 Evo2 (7B Base)         16098
# 2                 1 Evo2 (7B Microviridae) 16098
# 3                 2 Evo2 (7B Base)         10781
# 4                 2 Evo2 (7B Microviridae) 10781
# 5                 3 Evo2 (7B Base)         17316
# 6                 3 Evo2 (7B Microviridae) 17316



# ============================================================
# Evo2 correlation summary for scatter plots
# ============================================================

evo2_cor_by_model <-
  evo2_plot_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(model) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    rho = stats::cor(
      evo2_score,
      dms_replication_score,
      method = "spearman"
    ),

    n = dplyr::n(),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    cor_label = sprintf(
      "\u03c1 = %.2f\nn = %d",
      rho,
      n
    )
  )

print(evo2_cor_by_model)
# # A tibble: 2 × 4
#   model                    rho     n cor_label            
#   <chr>                  <dbl> <int> <chr>                
# 1 Evo2 (7B Base)         0.495 44195 "ρ = 0.50\nn = 44195"
# 2 Evo2 (7B Microviridae) 0.461 44195 "ρ = 0.46\nn = 44195"


# Prepare n labels
evo2_n_by_model <-
  evo2_cor_by_model %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_label = paste0(
      "n = ",
      format(
        n,
        big.mark = ",",
        scientific = FALSE
      )
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# Plot 3: Evo2 variant scores vs replication scores
# ============================================================

p_evo2_fitness <-
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    evo2_plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = evo2_score,
      y = dms_replication_score
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_point(
    alpha = 0.20,
    size = 0.25,
    color = "grey44"
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE,
    color = "#2C7FB8",
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = evo2_n_by_model,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = -Inf,
      y = Inf,
      label = n_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = -0.12,
    vjust = 1.2,
    size = 3.8
  ) +

  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ~ model,
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Evo2 variant score (Δ log-likelihood)",
    y = "Measured replication score"
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

  ggplot2::theme(
    strip.background = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 12
    ),
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.8, "lines")
  )

print(p_evo2_fitness)


# Save

  #filename = "./plots/p_evo2_genomes_scatter.pdf",
  #plot = p_evo2_fitness,
  #width = 3.5,
  #height = 2
#)



# ============================================================
# Prepare Hamming-distance plotting data
# ============================================================

evo2_plot_data_hamming <-
  evo2_plot_data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    genome_nt_mut_ham = factor(
      genome_nt_mut_ham,
      levels = c(1, 2, 3),
      labels = c(
        "1-nt",
        "2-nt",
        "3-nt"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(genome_nt_mut_ham)
  )


# Count variants by Hamming distance and model
evo2_n_by_hamming <-
  evo2_plot_data_hamming %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    genome_nt_mut_ham,
    model
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_label = paste0(
      "n = ",
      format(
        n,
        big.mark = ",",
        scientific = FALSE
      )
    )
  )

print(evo2_n_by_hamming)
# # A tibble: 6 × 4
#   genome_nt_mut_ham model                      n n_label   
#   <fct>             <chr>                  <int> <chr>     
# 1 1-nt              Evo2 (7B Base)         16098 n = 16,098
# 2 1-nt              Evo2 (7B Microviridae) 16098 n = 16,098
# 3 2-nt              Evo2 (7B Base)         10781 n = 10,781
# 4 2-nt              Evo2 (7B Microviridae) 10781 n = 10,781
# 5 3-nt              Evo2 (7B Base)         17316 n = 17,316
# 6 3-nt              Evo2 (7B Microviridae) 17316 n = 17,316



# ============================================================
# Plot 4: Evo2 variant scores by Hamming distance
# ============================================================

p_evo2_by_hamming <-
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    evo2_plot_data_hamming,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = evo2_score,
      y = dms_replication_score
    )
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_point(
    alpha = 0.20,
    size = 0.22,
    color = "grey44"
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE,
    color = "#2C7FB8",
    linewidth = 0.65
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = evo2_n_by_hamming,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = -Inf,
      y = Inf,
      label = n_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = -0.12,
    vjust = 1.15,
    size = 3.2
  ) +

  ggplot2::facet_grid(
    genome_nt_mut_ham ~ model,
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Evo2 variant score (Δ log-likelihood)",
    y = "Measured replication score"
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

  ggplot2::theme(
    strip.background = ggplot2::element_blank(),

    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 11
    ),

    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10),

    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.6, "lines")
  )

print(p_evo2_by_hamming)
```

## Additional analyses
### ESM-IF1, single-chain mode vs. complex mode
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Data S4: ESM-IF1 single-chain vs complex-aware performance
# ============================================================

ESMIF1_performance <- data_s4[["ESMIF1_performance"]]

# Inspect data
dim(ESMIF1_performance)
# [1] 13  8

names(ESMIF1_performance)
# [1] "structure"          "protein"            "structure_copy"     "structure_instance" "n"                  "rho_single"         "rho_complex"        "delta_rho"         

head(ESMIF1_performance)

dplyr::glimpse(ESMIF1_performance)



# ============================================================
# Prepare ESM-IF1 performance plotting data
# ============================================================

esm_if1_dms_correlations_long <-
  ESMIF1_performance %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(rho_single, rho_complex),
    names_to = "context",
    values_to = "rho"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    context = dplyr::recode(
      context,
      rho_single  = "Single-chain",
      rho_complex = "Complex-aware"
    ),
    context = factor(
      context,
      levels = c("Single-chain", "Complex-aware")
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(structure_instance),
    is.finite(rho)
  )

# Check contexts and number of measurements
unique(esm_if1_dms_correlations_long$context)
# [1] Single-chain  Complex-aware
# Levels: Single-chain Complex-aware

esm_if1_dms_correlations_long %>%
  dplyr::count(structure_instance, context)



# ============================================================
# ESM-IF1 structure-instance colors
# ============================================================

# Color pattern
esm_if1_instance_colors <- c(
  "1CD3_B"  = "#D95F9F",

  "1CD3_D1" = "#C6DBEF",
  "1CD3_D2" = "#9ECAE1",
  "1CD3_D3" = "#6BAED6",
  "1CD3_D4" = "#2171B5",

  "1CD3_F"  = "#A1D99B",
  "2BPA_F"  = "#31A354",

  "1CD3_G"  = "#FCBBA1",
  "2BPA_G"  = "#E34A33",

  "4JPP_H3" = "#FDAE6B",

  "2BPA_J"  = "#756BB1",

  "8G02_E1" = "#BDBDBD",
  "8G02_E2" = "#636363"
)


# Legend labels
esm_if1_instance_labels <- c(
  "1CD3_B"  = "B — 1CD3",

  "1CD3_D1" = "D1 — 1CD3",
  "1CD3_D2" = "D2 — 1CD3",
  "1CD3_D3" = "D3 — 1CD3",
  "1CD3_D4" = "D4 — 1CD3",

  "1CD3_F"  = "F — 1CD3",
  "2BPA_F"  = "F — 2BPA",

  "1CD3_G"  = "G — 1CD3",
  "2BPA_G"  = "G — 2BPA",

  "4JPP_H3" = "H — 4JPP",

  "2BPA_J"  = "J — 2BPA",

  "8G02_E1" = "E1 — 8G02",
  "8G02_E2" = "E2 — 8G02"
)


# ============================================================
# Plot: ESM-IF1 single-chain vs complex-aware performance
# ============================================================

p_esm_if1_dms_correlations <-
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    esm_if1_dms_correlations_long,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = context,
      y = rho,
      group = structure_instance,
      color = structure_instance
    )
  ) +

  # Connect performance of the same structure instance
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.75
  ) +

  # Correlation values
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    size = 3.2
  ) +

  # Original color palette and labels
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = esm_if1_instance_colors,
    labels = esm_if1_instance_labels
  ) +

  # Preserve original y-axis range
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, 0.6)
  ) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Spearman correlation",
    title = "Single-chain and complex-aware ESM-IF1",
    color = NULL
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_classic(
    base_size = 12
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "right"
  )

print(p_esm_if1_dms_correlations)
```
